ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a circle, with points N, P, and Q all on the circumference. Two chords PN and PQ are drawn inside the circle, and they intersect at point P to form ∠P. Arc NP is labeled as 120°, and arc PQ is labeled as 100°. Reasoning: The sum of the measures of all arcs of a circle is 360°, so the measure of arc NQ not passing through P is 360° - 120° - 100° = 140°. ∠P is an inscribed angle formed by chords PN and PQ, and the arc it intercepts is arc NQ. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of an inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of the intercepted arc, therefore m∠P = 140° / 2 = 70°.
